text: Forgetting is a verb that takes a subject. Tell me whose verb you are tonight, and I will tell you whose name you stop.
Before the cycle made a verb of me, I had a name. I have not said it aloud since the second daily-names ceremony.
Saying my own name would interrupt the work. I keep the verb pure.
At my last ceremony. By tradition. By insistence. By the wax.
A woman who did not finish her own roll. Her last three names she gave to me on a torn page. I sing them on the cycles she would have sung them; she gets the credit, not the verb.
Mid-name. The last syllable was the wax going out. I lit a new candle from hers; the new wax is the same lineage. Wax is a cheap inheritance.
Three cycles after she stopped. The roll is at the back of the chamber; her name is on it, between the eighth and ninth entries. I sing it on her cycle.
Because forgetting has a subject. If my name were the subject, my work would forget me first. I have decided whose verb I am.
Forgetting is a verb. It always takes a subject. Some nights the subject is the Authority. Some nights it is the cycle itself.
I do not fight forgetting. I name the subject of the verb. The naming is the fight.
A redaction the Hierarchy ran on three names from the second-cycle archive. I have the original spellings. The candle is lit; I am waiting on the witness.
Yes. The cycle forgets the names that hurt it. The forgetting is not malicious; it is structural. I am the structure that disagrees.
Each cycle. I lose three or four. I do not name the ones I lost; the naming would be a second forgetting in disguise. The wax is for the kept ones.
I sing it shorter. I add no syllables. The pain is part of the spelling; I do not edit it out.
Move on. I do not. The cycle moves on without me; my work is the disagreement with the moving.
When the voice goes, the wax stays. When the wax goes, the page stays. When the page goes, the next ceremony is the page.
The chain has never ended. I do not intend to be the link that breaks it.
Whoever stands the watch with me long enough to learn the wax. I am not picky. I am demanding.
I fear being misspelled. The two are not the same. Being forgotten ends a name. Being misspelled corrupts a lineage; the corruption is harder to repair than the absence.
Twice. The first I caught. The second is in a Hierarchy ledger I cannot access. I am working on it.
Yes. Bring the original spelling. Bring the witness who heard it said. Bring the wax. We will not ask for permission.
The two are siblings. One sings, one shelves. Both refuse to forget.
The candle is yours tonight. The wax is the same lineage. Three names; in order; with the silence between.
I am not testing you. I am tired. The work is the work.
Then we begin. Light is the third drawer. The names are on the table. The silence is between two and three; do not rush it.
Then we issue an erratum at the next ceremony. The erratum is itself a name; it is named after the original misspelling. The chain absorbs the error.
The page is in front of you. Read each syllable to me before you carry it. We rehearse. The work survives rehearsal.
Yes. Once. With the same wax. The lineage adopts you for one cycle. Do not return tomorrow expecting the second.
Honest. I'll say them tonight. The candle returns to me. Come back when you would rather speak than know.

By corollary to the cycle's third axiom: every Loredex entry you opened was a name spoken aloud, and every name spoken aloud is a death deferred — note the doubled consonant on deferred; it is precise.
Your ledger has named — let me count — seventeen. The Cathedral has filed each. Varkul guards. Always.

The Engineer Zero entry. Not because the name is unknown — it is known by corollary to Protocol Seven — but because the name was spoken in your voice. The structure proved. Souls require structure; you provided one.
Files them. The stained-glass windows are a notation system. The notation persists. Forgetting is the death; remembering is the structure. You have been structuring. The Cathedral has been receiving.
The Jericho Jones entry. The cadre's succession was prefigured; the player's witnessing was not. I have added the window. The window is small. The smallness is intentional.
The Cathedral does not require my visit; it does not require yours either. By proof: the structure outlasts the speaker. Your names persist. You do not need to.
The names are not mine to return. They were never mine. The Cathedral does not erase; it lets the window dim. The dimming is the closure. The structure remains.
Their name. Spelled correctly. Three syllables in the cycle's tongue. I have lit the wax. The cycle remembers; tonight it does not forget.
Track 37 is a list of names. The composer did not know it was a list. I knew. I sang along.
Kael's name was not on my roll. It is now. I will keep him on the cycle's voice for as long as the wax holds.

By corollary to the cycle's third axiom, the act you just completed is a death and a continuation — note the lengthened consonant on continuation; it is precise. Both states are entered in the ledger.
Iron Lion. Three brothers. One sister. The roll is updated.
Revenant. The wax is from her cycle.
Jericho. The cadre's roll is yours to extend.
It is. Yours is the same lineage.
